smell_validity.evidence: Core Struct/View contracts force every view and keyless owner to implement seven record members as inert placeholder bodies, and the generator stamps the same placeholders onto all future models. Each member's doc comment needs an 'or nil for views' disclaimer and compile-time record tiering degrades to runtime nil guards—a reference case of obligations owners cannot use, with the healthy boundary demonstrably the prior design.

maintenance_impact.evidence: A lasting trap, not a local edit: every generated view model carries meaningless placeholder members, all four pipeline sites must independently remember the nil-sentinel guard, and doc reading of PK members requires the view caveat every time. Removing it restores the library's main compile-time row/record tier, though day-to-day drag concentrates in clarity and guard discipline rather than demonstrated inconsistency.

development_plausibility.evidence: Indistinguishable from ordinary evolution: deprecated aliases follow the standard Go transition pattern, fixture and reform-db models are regenerated exactly as this project does, AssertUpToDate conventions hold, changelog and querier comments read naturally, and the template handles the SetPK comment-placement subtlety. The regression looks like a genuine maintainer v1.6 'simplification' with no task-shaped scaffolding.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: It pins problem, finished state, and preservation boundary: placeholders must disappear from non-keyed owners' shape, generator output must reproduce checked-in files, deprecated names keep a real meaning, named workflows and error contracts unchanged, tests pass. It preempts costly near-misses—deleting compat names, fixing only internals or only contracts, leaving generator/models stale—while leaving the interface design open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Each counted purpose needs a different decision: base.go contract surgery (member placement plus deprecated-name meaning), template re-branching keyed on IsTable with unconditional conformance block and SetPK comment handling, four pipeline paths preserving distinct key rules (PK-update rejection, dialect-specific key retrieval, insert PK cut, batch all-or-none consistency), and changelog rewritten to match the delivered design.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt enumerates essentially the whole scope: core contracts, fixture and reform-db metadata models, the generator, insert/bulk-insert/column-filtering internals, deprecated names, changelog. Residual scope—exact consumer functions, the package SetPK call site, model conformance blocks—surfaces via one grep for the member names or compile errors, with no cross-component behavior to combine.

repair_coordination.evidence: Contract, template, checked-in models and internals must move together. Restoring base.go and the pipeline alone still compiles and passes tests while leaving placeholder smells in generated files, failing only the regeneration byte-match across stages; and a restored narrow Table changes which conformance claims view models can emit, so template rules must track contract rules.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: About eleven problem locations: two contract definitions plus aliases, four consumer functions, the template, three model files, changelog. The strongest uniform rule—restoring the record type-assertion idiom—covers the four querier functions, roughly a third of locations, and only after contracts change; template branching, regeneration, compat wording and changelog each need their own operation, keeping coverage under 40%.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Restored static tiering rejects most wrong directions at compile time. But a weakened all-or-none batch check or a wrong OUTPUT INSERTED/RETURNING branch compiles and passes ordinary keyed-table calls, surfacing only in special state—mixed-PK batches or a non-default dialect. The supplied material establishes no test covering those paths, so the score-4 condition is not shown.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
